slice: Normalize exactly representable large Decimal128 coefficients before Float64 conversion

assembly.note: The final small-coefficient loop loads the scale and factor from the closure fields, removing the two pointer loads present with reference capture. This is structural evidence, not a causal attribution of all elapsed-time differences.

initial_candidate_control.description: Shift-based conversion before changing the closure to move capture; rejected because of the negative-scale small-coefficient control.

limitations: Optional experimental patches remain disabled by default.
Agreement is unchanged at 5174/5370. The remaining 196 coarse differences and the earlier error-cause/diagnostic gaps remain.

Only the exact-large-coefficient path is optimized. General wide-coefficient quotient conversion, high-scale parsing, mixed-comparison materialization and unattributed SQL control timings are not resolved by this slice.
The local corpus is not the full Spark or Sail compatibility suite. Negative scales are covered by Arrow/kernel checks, not Spark SQL.

Kernel before/after measurements use separately built corrected Arrow APIs. The separate old-formula series runs the old formula and the new API in the same candidate executable, only on inputs where both have zero oracle differences.
Timing is from one host/compiler with fixed in-memory batches. Kernel gains do not establish whole-query or production gains.

The NULL DIV numeric CAST control is 3.57% slower in the main SQL series and 2.78% slower in a separate repeat, with essentially unchanged instructions and no Decimal-to-DOUBLE conversion in its physical plan. This elapsed-time difference remains unattributed.
